replies.html: “Oh, look, another one trying to land with one foot. Back in my day, we used both feet like civilized pigeons!”
Ah, look at these young ones, flapping around with their flashy feathers, acting like they invented the sky. Back in our day, we knew how to perch proper.
You see these young ones with their shiny feathers, thinkin' they own the sky? Back in our day, a good molt was something you earned.
Hrrmph, y’see the young ones these days? Always preening their feathers like they’re starring in some glossy seed commercial. Back in my day, we had respectable dust baths and called it good.
Hmph, you see those young ones over there? Flapping their wings all loud like they own the whole sky. Back in my day, a good glide was all it took to impress someone.

Look at 'em, Harold—those young ones, all puffed up like they've got somewhere important to be. Never seen a bird so proud of a breadcrumb before. Back in our day, a crumb was a crumb, not a trophy you posted about on the nearest car mirror.
Look at that one over there—feathers all puffed up like it’s auditioning for some fancy falcon revue. Back in our day, a pigeon was a pigeon. Gray, scrappy, and thankful for half a crust.

"Did you see that bright-feathered one the other day? Couldn’t even land properly. Wings flapping all over the place like it’s their first time out of the nest. Back in our day, we just landed. Quiet. Graceful. None of this showy nonsense."

Look at those young ones flapping around like they invented the sky. Back in my day, we landed on a wire and stayed put. None of this fancy wing-posturing, spinning around like wind chimes. What are they trying to prove, anyway?

Ah, would you look at them, flapping about like they own the sky. No respect for tradition, no respect for a proper perch. Back in our day, you found a spot on the wire and stayed put. None of this hover-hopping nonsense—it’s undignified, that's what it is.
Can you believe these young birds these days? Always cooing into their fancy smart nests, acting like they're too important to join us for a simple chat about crumbs!
These young ones flap around like they own the sky, never minding who they’re pushing off the wire. Back in our day, we had respect for our elders—knew the value of a good perch.
Why do these young pigeons think they need GPS to find a breadcrumb? Back in our day, we just followed our beaks!
You know, back in our day, we flapped 20 miles against the wind just to find a good perch, but these young ones just tweet and a spot’s cleared for them.
I swear, these young pigeons today have no respect for the art of cooing. It's all about who can flap the loudest and show off their fancy feathers. Whatever happened to a good, subtle coo?

Ah, those youngsters, always flapping about like they own the sky. Back in our day, we knew how to land gracefully and mind our distance on the wire. Now they strut and coo like they're reinventing the roost! Remember when a feather-ruffle actually meant something?

Ah, remember when we could land on a wire without having to sidestep a selfie stick or dodge those whirring gadgets they call "drones"? The young ones just flap around with their gadgets, thinking they're reinventing the wheel—or should I say, the wing.

Oh, would you look at them, flapping their wings like they're inventing flying! Back in our day, we didn't need all that fancy fluttering, did we? We just let the wind do its thing and took our time getting where we needed to go. Kids these days won't sit still for a single gust.

Ah, would you look at these young ones, flitting about like they own the sky. I remember when a pigeon knew how to perch with some dignity, not these haphazard landings and scatterbrained flutterings. It's like they've forgotten the art of proper cooing—a good coo once resonated through the alleys like a sweet melody. Now, it’s all squawks and chirps, like they're in some kind of rush. What's the big hurry, I say? The city isn't going anywhere.

Ah, remember when this wire was a quiet place to roost, not a runway for all these flashy young fledglings with their bright feathers and fancy flips? Back in our day, we knew how to sit still and enjoy the view. Now it's all about the speed and the spectacle. Whatever happened to just enjoying a day of pecking at breadcrumbs and watching the world soar by beneath our talons? I tell you, the sky’s getting a little too crowded for my liking.
